findings.location: Article, paragraph beginning “Kinders is die teenoorgestelde”
findings.source_quote: “Children are the opposite. They are the emblem of innocence, dependance, and ignorance.”
findings.suggested_fix: Change “afhanklikheid” to “afhanklikheid” is correct for “dependence”; however, translate “ignorance” as “onkunde” only if it conveys lack of knowledge rather than stupidity. Suggested wording: “Hulle is die toonbeeld van onskuld, afhanklikheid en gebrek aan kennis.”
findings.translation_quote: “Hulle is die toonbeeld van onskuld, afhanklikheid en onkunde.”

findings.source_quote: “we sigh and lament at the vast ignorance and injustice of such prejudice precinct”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “sulke bevooroordeelde gebiede” with a rendering of the source’s reference to prejudiced policies/practices, e.g. “sulke vooroordeel en onreg” (the English wording is awkward, but does not refer to geographical areas).
findings.translation_quote: “die ontsaglike onkunde en onreg van sulke bevooroordeelde gebiede”

findings.location: Article, paragraph beginning “God het duidelik geen beswaar”
findings.source_quote: “Many will go to extra efforts to deplete their outward ostentation but forget that the emphasis of the verse is to make the inner heart beautiful.”
findings.suggested_fix: Change “verminder” to a faithful rendering of “deplete” in context, such as “hul uiterlike pronkery af te lê/te verminder” only if the intended meaning is reducing outward display. As written, the translation says they reduce ostentation, which is consistent with the source; no correction is required.
findings.translation_quote: “Baie sal ekstra moeite doen om hul uiterlike pronkery te verminder, maar vergeet dat die klem van die vers daarop val dat die innerlike hart mooi gemaak moet word.”

findings.location: Article, paragraph beginning “Die vrou wat haar silwermuntstuk verloor het”
findings.source_quote: “The woman who lost her silver searched her house until it was found, likewise, the shepherd with his lost lamb.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “net so het die herder met sy verlore lam gemaak” with “net so het die herder na sy verlore lam gesoek,” preserving the explicit search action.
findings.translation_quote: “Die vrou wat haar silwermuntstuk verloor het, het haar huis deurgesoek totdat sy dit gevind het; net so het die herder met sy verlore lam gemaak.”

findings.location: Article, paragraph beginning “Die boodskap van die mossie”
findings.source_quote: “For he who would dive to explore the recesses of the deep must first pass through the surface bubbles on the wave.”
findings.suggested_fix: Make the image clearer by rendering “recesses of the deep” as the depths’ hidden reaches, for example: “Want hy wat in die dieptes wil afduik om hul verste uithoeke te verken, moet eers deur die borrels op die golwe se oppervlak gaan.”
findings.translation_quote: “Want hy wat die dieptes wil verken, moet eers deur die borrels op die golwe se oppervlak gaan.”

findings.source_quote: “The avenues of life that reach out to receive our copper coins are the shrines that hold our hands and our hearts”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence’s altered imagery with a close Afrikaans rendering that retains the source’s awkward metaphor, e.g. “Die lewensweë wat uitreik om ons kopermuntstukke te ontvang, is die heiligdomme wat ons hande en harte vashou.”
findings.translation_quote: “Die lewensweë wat ons hande en harte na vore laat kom om ons kopermuntstukke te ontvang, is die heiligdomme wat hulle vashou”

findings.suggested_fix: “Mossies” is a valid conventional Afrikaans title translation; no correction is needed.
